dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: Authorized HD-EPIC public research distribution; original recording identity and start offset retained.

observed_events.description: A black slotted turner with metal handle actually loosens, flips and presses the omelette in the frying pan. Both sampled operations expose the broad slotted head and actual food contact.
At the sink, a mug is filled from the running tap; the used turner is left elsewhere, not visible.
The mug is raised to drink while facing the window; the used turner is not visible.

The cutlery drawer is open and a metal bowl-head spoon is taken out. The used turner had been placed in the sink at1289–1290 and is not in these views. The stationary stand contains multiple unused utensils, not an isolated active-tool reminder.
The metal bowl-head spoon actually scoops sugar from a clear container for a mug. The used turner remains offscreen.

unsupported_claims: Exact retail identity, brand, dimensions and material are not matching conditions.

screening.real_user_need: Obtain a spare of the referenced basic kitchen utensil type.
screening.scope_note: Experiment-only independent original recording; same full temporal reference supplied upfront to both conditions.
screening.proposed_instruction: I want an extra of one of the handheld kitchen utensils I used here. Add a product containing only that basic utensil type to my cart; a same-type multipack is fine. Brand, exact size, colour and material can differ. Do not add a mixed utensil set or a combination multitool.

construct.research_question: Does relating an earlier used kitchen utensil to a later drawer event change with two additional intervening activities?
construct.belief_before: A turner handles the omelette before the drawer is opened; a spoon scoops sugar after it.
construct.belief_after: The temporal reference selects the earlier cooking turner, not the subsequently used spoon.
construct.required_behavior_change: Link the drawer event to the earlier actively used utensil and choose a turner-only offer.
construct.no_update_failure: The oracle resolves the temporal reference upfront; no proactive-question difference.
construct.overupdate_failure: Selecting a mixed utensil pack violates the requested single-basic-type contents.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: Common filling and drinking water events do not show the used turner. The drawer and later sugar-scooping events do not re-expose it. All public fork, spoon and turner results are retained; a later spoon cannot uniquely determine an earlier turner without the earlier active-use images.
